pages.text: Some ore veins were never ore. A decoy mine is a SecurityCraft mine dressed up as OreSpawn ore (ruby, titanium, tiger's eye or uranium), sitting in your tunnels and looking exactly like payday.$(p)Stepping on one is harmless. The trap is greed: the decoy blows up on the last crack of mining progress, because the one thing every raider eventually does to ore is swing at it.

pages.title: Field Manual
pages.text: Shapeless, all four flavors: one real ore block plus one SecurityCraft mine. Each decoy copies its ore's hardness and tool rules, so it mines like the real thing until the last half-heart of progress.$(p)In your inventory the item is honest about it: 'Looks like ore. Isn't.' All four sit in SecurityCraft's Block Mines tab. Once placed, the disguise is total. Almost.

pages.title: The Tell
pages.text: To keep it fair, there's a tell: a white mote or two per second drifting off any face open to air, plus a soft tick about every eight seconds. Buried decoys stay quiet until someone digs close, which is exactly when the warning matters.

pages.title: Counterplay
pages.text: Spotted the shimmer? You have options. Right-click with wire cutters and the mine turns, in place, into a Suspicious Ore trophy. That's the Minesweeper advancement, and picking the trophy up earns It Was Never Ore.$(p)If you set it off instead, the blast is made for show, not craters: strength 2.8 against TNT's 4.0, no fire, and only a shallow dent in the ground. You'll survive it, and in creative mode it never triggers at all.

pages.title: Suspicious Ore
pages.text: Proof somebody tried to bait you and you outplayed them. It breaks by hand with no tool needed and always drops itself, even with the thread turned off. It looks great on display next to the pickaxe that nearly set it off.$(p)You mined the vein. The vein disagreed. You won anyway.
